body.en:
Paul sounds like a parent on a school morning: be very careful how you live — not as unwise, but as WISE, making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil! Don't be foolish, but understand what the Lord's will is.

Then comes the most important question: what fills you? Some people fill themselves with wine, which leads to losing control. Paul says instead: be filled with the SPIRIT — filled to the brim and overflowing with GOD!

The signs of being Spirit-filled? You overflow in speaking to one another with psalms, hymns, and songs from the Spirit — singing and making music from your HEART to the Lord — always giving thanks to God the Father for EVERYTHING, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

And then, submitting to one another out of reverence for Christ. A truly Spirit-filled life doesn't drain you — it overflows, in worship, in gratitude, and in genuine care for others.

verse.en: Instead, be filled with the Spirit, speaking to one another with psalms, hymns, and songs from the Spirit.

title.en: A Song for Wake Up and Sing

q.en: What does Paul say to be filled with, instead of wine?
What overflows when a person is truly filled with the Spirit?
What does Paul say believers should do out of reverence for Christ?

label.en: Activity sheet: Wake Up and Sing

body.en:
Big idea: the Spirit-filled life is marked by overflow, not depletion — worship, gratitude, music, and mutual submission flowing naturally from a heart filled with God rather than substitutes. "Making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil" (5:16) gives urgency without anxiety: wise, alert living, not fearful living.

Conversation starters: (1) What things do people try to "fill" themselves with, instead of the Spirit? (2) Why might singing and gratitude be such natural signs of being Spirit-filled? (3) What does mutual submission "out of reverence for Christ" look like in your family?

Pray together for a fresh filling of the Holy Spirit, overflowing in worship and gratitude.
